name: Drusilla (Felix' wife, daughter of Agrippa I)
title: Jewish princess and Roman governor's wife
summary: Drusilla was the daughter of King Herod Agrippa I and sister to Agrippa II and Berenice. She left her first husband to marry the Roman governor Felix, and was present when Paul made his defense in Caesarea.

keyEvents.title: Hears Paul's defense speech
keyEvents.description: Drusilla was present with her husband Felix when Paul spoke about faith in Christ Jesus. Felix became frightened as Paul talked about righteousness, self-control, and the coming judgment.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as a Jewess
keyEvents.description: The Bible describes Drusilla as a Jewess, which highlights her Herodian royal lineage and connection to the Jewish people, even though she was married to a pagan Roman official.
